title: performance(canary): enhance auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions and rollout guards
author: Maya Patel
commits: Add adaptive thresholding module for canary detector (canary_detector.py)
Introduce sequence-length and model-profile aware baselines (models/thresholds.json)
Integrate throughput regression detection into rollout guard policy (infra/rollout-guards/policy.yaml)
Add instrumentation and new canary metrics (observability/metrics/canary_metrics.sql)
Add integration test and CI job for perf canary regression detection (tests/integration/test_canary_regression.py)
Docs: perf canary behavior, tuning guide, and rollout guard examples (docs/perf_canary.md)
description: Context: Our performance canary pipeline detects latency regressions but has had blind spots for throughput regressions and model/sequence-length specific behavior. This PR extends the canary detector with adaptive thresholds, throughput anomaly detection, and tighter rollout guards so that launches can fail fast on real regressions while avoiding noisy false positives. Changes: 1) Add an adaptive thresholding module that computes baseline distributions per model, instance-type, and dominant sequence-length buckets; baselines are stored in services/perf-canary/models/thresholds.json. 2) Add throughput regression detection (p99/sec and sustained qps) in canary_detector.py with configurable windowing and hysteresis to avoid flapping. 3) Wire throughput and latency detectors into infra/rollout-guards/policy.yaml so canary results can block automatic rollouts; introduce a soft-fail path (canary->monitoring) for canary experiments under low traffic. 4) Add new canary metrics and dashboard queries in observability/metrics/canary_metrics.sql to support root-cause analysis and automated alerting. 5) Add integration tests and a dedicated CI job (ci/ci-jobs/canary_integration.yml) that runs a synthetic workload to validate detection behavior under regressions and noise. 6) Update docs/perf_canary.md with tuning guidance and examples. Testing: Local unit tests updated; integration job failed initially due to race in test harness, fixed by adding deterministic seeding and a 2s warmup in test_canary_regression.py. CI: initial run failed on flaky test, re-run passed; full pipeline green. Rollout: This was merged to main with a squash merge after approvals and green CI. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve existing canary behavior unless the adaptive thresholds feature flag is enabled. Risk/impact: Moderate — changes affect canary detection logic and rollout blocking. We added feature flags and safe default policy to avoid customer impact. Follow-ups: ENG-2570 to add automatic baseline refresh job and ENG-2699 to support model-variant specific thresholds.
review_comments: Ethan Wu: Nice work. Can you add a short explanation in the docs for how hysteresis is computed? Also request to add a unit test that simulates transient spikes.

Maya Patel: Added hysteresis explanation to docs and a transient spike unit test in tests/unit/test_hysteresis.py in a follow-up commit. The integration test already validates no-flap behavior with a 90s observation window.
Sofia Martinez: Is there a danger of overfitting thresholds to the synthetic workload? Suggest adding a minimum sample floor and cross-validation with historical production windows.
Maya Patel: Agreed. Added minimum-sample-size check and a config option to disable model-specific overrides. Filing follow-up ENG-2699 to add automated cross-val job.
Hector Alvarez: CI was flaky on first run due to test harness timing; confirm stability before merging.
Maya Patel: Fixed the harness by seeding and adding warmup; reran CI and job passed.
release_notes: Enhances performance canary detection with adaptive thresholds and throughput regression detection; adds rollout guard integration and instrumentation. Feature is behind a feature flag by default.
